cross: Each pair crosses starter 0/1 and physical position swap false/true. Self:192 new games. Panel:256 new games, target actor0 and opponent actor1; both starts and both physical seats are crossed, without redundant actor-label duplication. Target D and D-walk use identical seed/RNG and opponents.

tieDevelopment.source: eight original D-unresolved checkpoints from b-factorial

tieHoldout.source: one new D/D trajectory per self seed, swap=false starter=0. First pre-move state with ply>=16 and quiet>=8, else first ply>=12, else last pre-move state. No variant outcomes used for selection; exclude physical duplicates and development states.

statistics.unit: seed block, preserving paired roles and positions
primary: D-walk self settlement minus D self settlement
mixed D-walk versus D observed win-indicator difference
statistics.secondary: Paired observed wins and settlement versus each fixed panel opponent, exploratory. Unresolved always separate. Report all observed prefix lengths plus censoring bounds and restricted mean plies at horizon256.

adoption: No default/production promotion unless independent self settlement improves robustly, mixed strength lower95% net-win difference is above -0.10, panel safety/strength does not show material worsening and resource cost is acceptable. The 0.10 tolerance is an exploratory screening threshold, not established noninferiority. Human fun and real-device performance untested. Tie variants are diagnostics, not automatically adopted.

longGameTags.note: Descriptive tags, not new stopping rules or proof of forced defense

limits: Protocol fixed in local Git before new outcomes, not external preregistration
Old continuations, new games, checkpoint forks and AI replays counted separately
Time/plies/memory caps remain unresolved, never official draws
Parallel workers share 8CPU/8GiB host; timing and cumulative RSS descriptive
All tie variants keep D root set, RNG, original leaf evaluator and unequal root values
No official rules, board, src, production CPU, images, modes A-E, merge or deployment changes
